Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It's the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it's a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There's plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies greets Kaleb Spencer #3 before the game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven't rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que'Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he's secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds' 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren't as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don't incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he's tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies' defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It's a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven't been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 17: Southern Methodist University Mustangs defensive end Marques White (16) rushes the passer during the game between SMU and Virginia on October 17, 2026 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs' fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee's team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs' kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven't scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they've won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU's offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs' receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU's first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday's loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU's defense didn't necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse's fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they're the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU's discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Prediction: SMU 30, Virginia Tech 24

picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions Stike up the Hokie Pokey, Tech Triumph, and the Victory Tag. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:59 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a short week after a week break. The Hokies are heading to Dallas to face off against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs. The Hokies are up against another major ACC opponent, and winning the game means advancing in the ACC and potentially seeing a ranking. Crossover Week Mayhem Just a note from us: Well, the first week in November through the first week of December is always a challenge for coverage. The soccer teams are wrapping up with decent enough records, but their seasons aren't quite over. The Women's Basketball Team has opened their home record at 2-0, and the Men's team also graced Cassell with a W. All of that puts a real strain on coverage so bear with us as we sort out schedules, and fight fall health issues and work vs. Hokie sports balance. The football team isn't finished, though. There are still four games left on the schedule, and then we get to plan on bowl coverage this season. Isn't that a happy event? The Hokies are bowl eligible just a couple of games after the halfway point, and that's a very pleasant occurrence. To think that we are actually paying attention to the bowl invitation list, instead of worrying on Thanksgiving weekend whether or not a win will net an invitation somewhere. The first thing to cover is a bit of fun. The ACC Network desk hosts Eric McClain and Eddie Royal had a bet going. Remember, McClain is a former Clemson player, and we all know and love Eddie Royal. So, the bet was that the loser had to wear the winner's mascot costume. Eddie was not dressed as a Tiger with the googly eyes for the TV segment. ( Congratulations to the Virginia Tech Cheer Squad equipment folks and Travis Wells for getting most of an actual Hokie Bird big enough for Eric. ) The Virginia Tech Wrestling Team received a massive boost from a wrestler who hasn't even wrestled his first match as a Hokie, yet, but who is already a world champion. Freshman Bo Bassett traveled to Kazakhstan and netted the program its first world championship and was the first American in 20 years to win in his weight class (65KG – for those lacking metric conversion skills that's 143 pounds ). The Coach Robie is going to have an absolutely dominant wrestling team this season. Back to Football Stuff It looks like the team is going to be wearing head to toe all-whites for this one. Go get your coffee, or a quick snack and listen in on Coach Franklin's weekly presser. As Bryan posted up earlier, this time the Hokies have some really good news coming out of the locker room as it pertains to the Offensive Line. Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back up to speed and are expected to play on Friday night. The O-Line has been dipping into the #3s on the depth chart for the past few games, and getting them back is a serious update to the struggling run game. That All Leads to This… Predictions The SMU Mustangs are largely a Big XII import with a near automatic bubble to the top of the ACC football pile. It's Dallas, TX, and football is a near religion for Texas. That means the program is well funded, with premium coaching, and players doused liberally with NIL funding. Up until last weekend, the Mustangs were sporting a very respectable one loss record. Until they showed up in the Syracuse (whatever they call the Carrier Dome, now), as expected in the beginning of the season SMU was challenging hard for the #2 bid in the ACC fake Championship game ( until the conference goes back to divisions and division champs who play everyone else in the division the game in Charlotte will remain fake to me ). Then the Mustangs got treated to the old Big East upset win by the Orange. That knocked them down a peg but also put the Hokies in the position of earning the #3 spot on the ACC leader board. That all means that this game might not mean an ACC bid, but it will mean a much better bowl game situation over the holidays. Bowls mean big broadcast money, and the program needs the cash to make up for a restricted gate at Lane. The Mustangs are favored by slightly less than a touchdown for this one, in their house no less. We'll see how we feel about that. This is a big test for the Hokies. Virginia Tech had a huge win at Clemson two weeks ago. No, this isn't the same Clemson team as only a few years ago, but it means something for other ACC teams to walk into Death Valley and win. SMU is better than the Tigers, but they aren't unbeatable. The clear difference here is the quarterback position. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings is a stud. He also has one of the ACC's best running backs and one of the top receiving units in the league. This is a huge challenge for VT defensive coordinator Brent Pry. Offensively, I think the Hokies have success moving the ball. SMU's size on the defensive interior concerns me, especially with Tech's OL struggles. There is hope that with Cunningham and Meadows back, the offensive line is better, but we'll see. I expect a close game. My heart says the Hokies, my head says SMU in a close one. SMU 34, Hokies 31 This game all depends on how the Mustangs adjusted to their Syracuse loss, and if the Hokies on both sides of the ball can adjust to how the Orange controlled the SMU offense, and how they managed to get by their defense. SMU, interestingly enough, has a similar offensive/defensive balance to Tech's than we have seen this season. There are lots of "IFs" in this game, and the biggest one is "IF" the Tech defense can limit the SMU offense to what it's been scoring over the season against peer teams, the Hokies have a much better chance to win than the listed 6-point betting gimme to SMU. The latest projected O/U is 56.5, which tells me volumes of information. The analysts see this as a very close game, and the end result being less than a full score between the two teams. If the Hokies stay away from getting enamored of the run game and go downfield fast and consistently in the air on quick developing intermediate routes to their best receivers, there will be run opportunities. If Tech decides to try to "establish the run" the offense could bog down into chronic 3-and-outs. The return of two key #1/#2 depth chart players is not an excuse to try to revert to 1960's caveman Johnny Unitas two runs and a pass offense. If the Hokies move the ball and do it fast, they have enough defense ( which needs to put serious pressure on the quarterback on every play ) to hold the Mustangs to a 3.5 score effort. The Hokies are capable of 4 or more. That's a whole lot of "Ifs" though. Here's the skinny… the first team to score over 30 points wins. That puts my prediction hat on, and I think the Hokies might just be good for it, regardless of the conditions. Just a quick reminder of the times and broadcast information. It's an ESPN deal.

Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. Sophomore Tyren Polley Jr., third on the team with 34 tackles, tore a pectoral muscle in October and is out for the season. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. Jeffrey Overton Jr. snaps his 100-yard drought Overton last reached 100 yards on Sept. 26, when he ran for 209 at Boston College, the sixth-highest single-game total in Virginia Tech history. He has 230 yards in four games since and averaged 2.6 yards per carry at Clemson. The sophomore still leads the Hokies with 639 yards on 113 carries. Two things change Friday. The first is the offensive line. "We're going to get some guys back, which is helpful, especially on the offensive line," coach James Franklin said Monday. Guard/tackle Montavious Cunningham and guard Brody Meadows are expected to play. Left tackle Justin Terry is still out. The second is the defense across from him. SMU allows 125.9 rushing yards per game and 3.8 yards per carry. Those numbers flatter the Mustangs. College football counts sacks as rushing plays, and SMU has 23 sacks for 148 yards. Pull them out, and opponents are averaging 4.8 yards per designed run. Those 23 sacks matter for Virginia Tech in another way. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been sacked 23 times himself. A run game that works keeps the Hokies on schedule and gives SMU's rushers something else to think about. Overton gets his third 100-yard game of the season. 3. Virginia Tech sacks Kevin Jennings at least four times Before Halloween, SMU hadn't allowed more than two sacks in a game this season. Syracuse got six. Look at who was playing on the left side. True freshman Drew Evers moved over from right tackle to start at left tackle, and fellow true freshman Sam Utu made his first career start beside him at left guard. It was only the second college game of his career. SMU could get some help back. Guard Alex Woods, a starter, missed Syracuse, and tackle Andrew Chamblee, who has started at both tackle spots, hasn't played since Oct. 17. Neither is on Thursday's availability report. Watch the first series to see who lines up on the left. Either way, Virginia Tech has the rushers to test it. The Hokies average 3.4 sacks per game, sixth in FBS, and three players have more than four: Aycen Stevens with eight, Cortez Harris with five and Mylachi Williams with 4.5. Defensive tackle Kemari Copeland said this week the plan is to "cage" Jennings and take away his scrambles to the right. Friday, the Hokies get to Jennings at least four times. picks.blurb: How Bear Bachmeier's four INTs doomed Cougars in Holy War loss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers How Bear Bachmeier's four INTs doomed Cougars in Holy War loss Craig Meyer, USA TODAY NETWORK · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:03 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The rivalry between Utah and BYU isn't just a football game. It's a war — a Holy War, to be exact. This year, the ramifications of that Biblical clash were larger than they've ever been, at least in recent memory. And it was the Utes who were able to come away with a victory. Watch BYU vs. Utah football live with Fubo (free trial) In one of the most anticipated games of a loaded Week 10 slate of the 2026 college football season, quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four total touchdowns, two rushing and two passing, to lift No. 4 Utah to a 28-20 victory over No. 8 BYU on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, Utah. The win was sealed with two seconds remaining, when Nate Ritchie intercepted a Bear Bachmeier desperation heave in the end zone. It was Bachmeier's fourth interception of the day, matching the BYU quarterback's total from his team's first eight games this season. More: Utah has a message for CFP, SEC and Big Ten: Deal with us now The turnovers proved to be costly on a day in which the Cougars outgained the Utes by a 391-328 margin and averaged 6.1 yards per play. The win kept Utah's unbeaten record intact, improving the Utes to 9-0 overall and 6-0 in the Big 12 heading into a big game next week at No. 22 Arizona. The victory snapped Utah's three-game Holy War losing streak and was their first win in the rivalry since 2019. BYU, meanwhile, fell to 7-2 overall and 4-2 in the Big 12, narrowing its path to the Big 12 championship game and a spot in the College Football Playoff. Get real-time updates, scoring plays, turning points and expert analysis throughout as BYU takes on Utah. Follow along as USA TODAY Sports provides live updates, highlights, injury news, key plays and instant breakdown from the Cougars-Utes showdown. Utah-BYU analysis As painful as it would have been, Utah could have afforded to withstand a loss to BYU, thanks to an 8-0 start to the season that gave coach Morgan Scalley's team enough cushion to make a Big 12 championship game or College Football Playoff appearance even without an unbeaten record. But after three losses in a row to the Cougars in a series in which they hadn't won since 2019, the Utes really needed this one. And even beyond the bragging rights they earned with a 28-20 victory, they got a win that will resonate. With just three games remaining in the regular season, Utah is 9-0, with only one game left against a team that's in the top 25 of the US LBM Coaches Poll. Thanks to the win over the Cougars — which was made possible at least in some part by Bear Bachmeier's four interceptions — the Utes have a two-game lead for the second and final spot in the Big 12 championship game. To make things sweeter, by beating BYU, they significantly narrowed the Cougars' playoff chances, though a road to the 12-team field is certainly there. A big win in front of a home crowd to boost your own championship aspirations while putting your hated foes' on life support? It's what rivalry dreams are made of. And today, Utah gets to live them. Bear Bachmeier grade The BYU quarterback made some plays when he needed to and played a key role in helping the Cougars withstand an early 14-point deficit to score 20 unanswered points. His 75-yard touchdown pass to Legend Glasker in the second quarter was a thing of beauty. Beyond that, Bachmeier had a nightmarish game. The sophomore was the primary reason why a team that racked up nearly 400 yards and averaged 6.1 yards per play is nursing the wounds of a rivalry loss. Bachmeier threw four interceptions, matching his total from his first eight games this season. Each of his four picks came in Utah territory, two of which were in the Utes' red zone and one of which was on a third-and-goal from the 2-yard line with 4:39 remaining that, had he not made that mistake, would have given his team one more shot at a potential game-tying touchdown. Devon Dampier grade In some ways, Dampier was the opposite of Bachmeier. His overall stat line wasn't particularly impressive. He completed only 54% of his passes (though he was the victim of several drops by his wideouts), averaged just 6.8 yards per attempt and threw for nearly 100 fewer yards than his BYU counterpart. But he was an absolute force on the ground, racking up a game-high 87 yards and giving his team a reliable option to pick up yards when the passing game wasn't working. He accounted for each of Utah's four touchdowns, with two rushing and two passing scores. He even came up with an impressive catch on a trick play on a fourth-and-1 from the BYU 45-yard line. Given the emotions going into this game, the unusual kickoff time, and Utah's track record of strong starts, BYU needs to weather the early storm at Rice Eccles Stadium. If BYU can settle in and adjust to Utah's unique offense, the Cougars will have a great chance to pull off the upset. BYU is expected to get LJ Martin back in the lineup for the first time since early October against TCU. How effective and how healthy Martin will be remains to be seen. On offense, Bear Bachmeier will have to carry another heavy load. Bachmeier will have chances to throw from clean pockets against a Utah defense that will give up explosive plays through the air. Bachmeier and his wide receivers, particularly deep threat Legend Glasker, need to have a big game. BYU is the best defense Utah will have faced by a wide margin. Even though the BYU defense has struggled to bring ball-carriers to the ground, we like their chances to keep the Utah offense somewhat in check. Like it usually does, this game will come down to the wire. When it does, we like Bear Bachmeier's chances to find a way to win in the fourth quarter. Here is how I'm wagering college football Week 10. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . No. 9 BYU @ No. 3 Utah This Holy War might be the holiest of them all: Utah hosting bitter rival BYU, with the winner in the driver's seat for a Playoff spot. It’s the first time both teams have been ranked in the top 10 for this matchup, and I can’t wait to start the day with this one. I think BYU might win outright. It has been tested with its win over Notre Dame just a few weeks ago. Yes, it lost to UCF the following week in a typical trap game — big home win followed by a road conference game. Otherwise, the Cougars have handled business, even though the scores don’t seem that impressive. BYU is built on defense. It is 13th in yards per play and it limits explosives. It does not rush the passer all that well, but against Utah’s rushing attack, that might not be needed. BYU’s defense already faced a high-powered offense in the Irish and limited it to a negative EPA rushing day. Utah’s offensive production slowly ticked down when conference play started, but it did bounce back last week against a poor Cincinnati defense. Utah has played one defense in the same realm as BYU and that was Houston. Utah struggled to score, only putting up 21 points with seven of those happening super late after forcing a Houston turnover. Will the BYU offense find a groove against Utah? (Getty Images) It’s fair to also believe BYU’s offense might struggle in this game. However, it appears the Cougars are getting stud running back LJ Martin back, and they are much better when Martin is on the field. He’s averaging almost eight yards a carry with 20% of his rushes going for 10+ yards. Utah’s defense is the typical physical front against the run, but BYU is the best offense the Utes have faced all season. Utah’s pass rush concerns me. It is 80th in pressure rate and unless it blitzes, it isn't able to get to the quarterback. Seems less than ideal against BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier. I see these teams as even. They are both defensively based with an offense that wants to run the ball. That’s too many points in a game like this. I’ll take BYU to cover. Schwartz's Pick: BYU -4.5 No. 5 Alabama @ No. 14 LSU In the newly-released CFP rankings, Alabama is fifth and is an underdog at LSU by almost a touchdown. I do lean towards LSU at -6, but that number feels big. Instead, I’m going to fade Alabama’s offense in this game. Alabama is facing its fourth straight difficult defense, and in the first three games, we’ve seen the offensive efficiency drop. Quarterback Keelon Russell is nearing the end of his first season as a starting quarterback, and he’s been mostly excellent for his age. However, he has struggled the last three weeks outside the end of the Texas A&M game. Against Georgia, Tennessee and A&M, he completed only 60% of passes with just four passing touchdowns and three interceptions. Alabama’s beat-up offensive line has allowed 11 sacks in the three previous games. Now, the Tide play an LSU defense that’s first in sacks per pressure and 11th in pressure rate. The Bama offensive line and Russell were noticeably affected by the environment in Tennessee, and now they are at LSU. I feel most comfortable with Alabama not scoring much in this game. Klatt's Week 10 Picks Updated Nov. 5, 2026 11:36 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link The long-awaited, top-25-filled Week 10 of the college football season is finally here. Everything from College Football Playoff implications to potential conference championship matchups are in play this Saturday. Starting at 12 p.m. ET, No. 9 BYU heads to No. 3 Utah for the annual Holy War rivalry matchup, with instant CFP and Big 12 title impact. The day ends with No. 1 Miami at No. 11 Notre Dame in a rematch of the game that arguably kept the Fighting Irish out of last year's CFP. Especially after Tuesday's first CFP rankings of the season — which FOX Sports' Joel Klatt raised concerns about — this weekend's slate will make a heavy impact on the postseason playoff picture. Here at Klatt's Week 10 picks and previews, from the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show": No. 1 Miami (Fla.) vs. No. 11 Notre Dame (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: Notre Dame -5.5 Moneyline: Notre Dame -238, Miami +195 Klatt's thoughts: " Notre Dame, you got to win … The committee really put Notre Dame behind the eight ball. They're backed into a corner. So, don't we all expect to get Notre Dame's best? I mean, we have to … Now, Miami has taken care of business. Notre Dame did not. They got beat by BYU. Yes, there was a second left. They didn't get that snap, and so here they are with their backs against the wall. "Let's take a look at this game from just like: what's the strongest thing? What's the weakest thing that any of these teams do? Well, if you're looking at the weakest thing, I always look at that, because in a matchup game typically the weakest link of the teams is what's going to end up getting you beat, and the weakest thing that anybody does in this game is Miami's defense, and we've seen that over the last, what, three weeks and three games. Two of the last three games, they've given up 35 points to Florida State and UNC. So it's not a great defense. It is not nearly the defensive front that they had a year ago. Their secondary is not great. "So they've got to find a way to limit CJ Carr, who I think is one of the better quarterbacks that we have in the country. What's the strongest part of this game? It's Miami's offense. It's interesting. They've got the strongest part. They've got the weakest part. Their ceiling with their offense is outstanding. I think it's the best thing anybody does in college football. Darian Mensah film is fantastic. I love watching it. "I'm going to go to Notre Dame. I think that they have to win, and they will win because, again, the committee is doing Miami no favors here … Notre Dame 30-27. Miami, I'll take the 5.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Notre Dame Klatt's pick against the spread: Miami +5.5 No. 9 BYU vs. No. 3 Utah (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Utah -4.5 Moneyline: Utah -198, BYU +164 Klatt's thoughts: "BYU at Utah. Holy War. 4.5 is the spread here. Utah is favored. Utah has lost three straight in this series, including a home game. BYU has not looked great since the Notre Dame game. I think we would all agree with that. Utah has been a team that has been very impressive, which is largely why they're ranked No. 3 in the country right now. Because even though they've played something north of a wet paper bag, the committee decided that they were the third-ranked team in the country. That was a shot. It wasn't meant to be a shot. Because I love Utah. You know I love you, Utah. Death, taxes, Utah football. They roared back against Houston after being down 10-0 at around halftime. They destroyed Cincinnati. They're a difficult team to beat on the road when they're in their home stadium. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker are dynamic. The one concern I would have for Devon Dampier is the turnovers. "You can't do that in this game, not in this game. And, in particular, with an aggressive BYU defense … They're going to have to run the football, play quality defense, and use the energy of that stadium to their benefit. LJ Martin for BYU could be back. I don't know how effective he will be, but they need that because they have not been able to run the football very well over the last couple of weeks. Speaking of BYU, both have good defenses. Although, gosh, you know I love Kalani Sitake. I think Kalani Sitake is fantastic, but his defense the last couple of weeks hasn't been like BYU standard. I personally believe this Utah team has something to prove. Almost like their coach retired and then took another job somewhere else. It's like it resembles that. I don't know if that was the case or not, but that's what it looks like. And Morgan Scalley has been there for a long time, and he understands the culture of Utah. And I think this team is playing with an edge. " Utah 27, BYU 20. Utah covers the 4.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Utah Klatt's pick against the spread: Utah -4.5 No. 2 Georgia vs. No. 10 Ole Miss (Photo by Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) Spread: Georgia -3.5 Moneyline: Georgia -175, Ole Miss +145 Klatt's thoughts: "Georgia at Ole Miss. This one could be a great game. I really think it could be. Georgia is favored by 3.5. Rematch to that quarterfinal from a year ago. Ole Miss won that one. Trinidad Chambliss was outstanding in that ball game, and I'm sure Kirby Smart has had nightmares about Trinidad Chambliss ever since then. And now he's got to go to Oxford, and he's got to play Trinidad Chambliss where Trinidad Chambliss has never lost a start. Ole Miss is not going to have Kewan Lacy, he's likely out in this game. Trinidad Chambliss is a guy that I love. You guys, I know I've loved him ever since the beginning of the year, and now he gets to face Kirby Smart. And this team is the best road team that we have in the country over the last several years. Why? Because they're consistent. Why? Because they run the football. Because they play good defense. These are the things that travel. These are the things that allow you to have success on the road. I do think it's going to be a close game. I don't think Georgia is going to be able to separate in this game, but they're too consistent. They're too consistent. "If Georgia can hold Ole Miss to field goals, I think that's where the game is won or lost. If it's high scoring, I favor Ole Miss because Trinidad runs wild. If it's lower scoring and in the 20s, then I favor Georgia because it's a slug fest, and you're kicking field goals, and it's third down and it's situations. What do I think it's going to be? More of a slug fest. "I'm going to take Georgia 28-24 . They cover the 3.5 on the road." Klatt's straight-up pick: Georgia Klatt's pick against the spread: Georgia -3.5 No. 23 Oregon vs. No. 12 Ohio State (Photo by Melinda Meijer/ISI Photos/Getty Images) Spread: Ohio State -7.5 Moneyline: Ohio State -305, Oregon +245 Klatt's thoughts: " Oregon at Ohio State . Ohio State favored by 7.5. Interesting. So Vegas likes Ohio State a lot more than the committee does. By the way, Oregon has a path to the Big Ten championship game. I know we haven't talked about that a lot on this program, but I know other programs have mentioned it. Yes, that's absolutely the case. And if I were Oregon, I would smell the blood in the water a little bit. "This is not the same Ohio State that came into Eugene a couple of years ago and would eventually win the national championship. And it is certainly not the same Ohio State that you saw in the Rose Bowl, and that kind of, you know, blew the hinges off in that game. I don't know what we're going to get. Luke Fahey is going to start at QB again. How long is the leash for Luke Fahey? Not sure. I don't think he played very well … I thought the ball went to the wrong spot a few times. He overthrew some open wide receivers, and they didn't get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. "Jay Johnson is [Oregon's] new offensive coordinator after they fired Drew Mehringer after that Illinois game, and they looked a lot better in the second half against Northwestern. This is a very different defense than they're going to face. I think this is a much better secondary, and I would think that Matt Patricia of Ohio State is going to find a way to put pressure on Dylan Raiola. He does not deal with pressure well. It's like Ohio State's backed into a corner … You just get all of Ohio State, and if you get all of Ohio State, that means that you get all of Jeremiah Smith , and they're going to be taking shots, and they're going to be more aggressive even with a young quarterback, because you got nothing to lose. "I'm going to say Ohio State wins this game. They have to. They win it 30-20 . They cover the 7.5." Klatt's straight-up pick: Ohio State Klatt's pick against the spread: Ohio State -7.5 No. 5 Alabama vs. No. 14 LSU (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Spread: LSU -5.5 Moneyline: LSU -225, Alabama +185 Klatt's thoughts: " Alabama at LSU , always a great game. LSU is favored by 5.5 over the committee's fifth-ranked team. You mean Vegas doesn't agree with the committee either? No, they don't. No one does. Literally, no one. Not even Bama fans … Bad matchup for Alabama in this one. I think it's a terrible matchup for Alabama. Let me tell you why, because if Kalen DeBoer gets into a big game, typically they throw the football a lot and they don't run it very well. And when that happens, they have to protect their quarterback. And if they can't protect their quarterback, they don't win. And LSU is a terrific pass rushing team. Terrific, second in the country in sacks. Meanwhile, you would think that Alabama on the offensive line would do a good job protecting their quarterback. Not the case. We saw pressure against Tennessee, pressure against Georgia, and LSU might be better in the pass rush than both of those teams. Bad matchup. I don't think they're going to be able to run the football. "Speaking of Alabama … They beat Mississippi State, who was undefeated at the time. Each of the last two times that they played LSU in Death Valley, Alabama has been held under 70 yards rushing, and that's even with better Alabama teams and teams that are more willing to run the football. So again, all of this leads to: Do I think LSU can at least get out of their own way offensively, not turn the football over and score some points? The answer is yes. Sam Leavitt is playing better. He's taking care of the ball … You've got some guys back for Alabama. I don't know how much they're going to give you. Ryan Coleman-Williams is going to be back. Zabien Brown might be back. I just think LSU, they're going to be a team that's going to be very difficult to beat in this one. I've got LSU 30, Alabama 17. LSU covers the 5.5" Klatt's straight-up pick: LSU Klatt's pick against the spread: LSU -5.5 No. 7 Texas vs. Missouri (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Spread: Texas -2.5 Moneyline: Texas -142, Missouri +120 Klatt's thoughts: " Texas at Missouri. This one should be an interesting game, partly because I have no idea who's going to be playing for Texas. They are a mess unit right now. Sark has come out and talked about them being a bit undermanned this week. Let me just roll through a couple of these. Sark put it this way: could be without Cam Coleman, could be without Ryan Wingo, already without Trevor Goosby, their left tackle. Will be without Hollywood Smothers, all on offense. Two starting corners look like they're going to be out. Colin Simmons' status unknown. Best pass rusher in college football, week-to-week with that ankle. He's missed the last two. Who's going to be out there? Arch Manning is going to be out there. What do I worry about with Texas? That it becomes an Arch show. Because when it's an Arch show, it's not great. "We've been

the year takes place this Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium between #9 BYU (7-1) and #3 Utah (8-0). It’s the Holy War! Both teams sit atop the Big 12, and the winner of this game is likely in the Big 12 Championship, whereas the loser can’t afford another loss to make the conference title game. Utah is enjoying its highest ranking in program history, and depending on what happens this weekend, the Utes could end up No. 1. Devon Dampier has led an electric offense averaging 38.9 points per game (11th) in their first year without Kyle Whittingham and with Morgan Scalley at the helm; but the defense has been incredible! The Utes have been a tank from the start. Utah averages 10.3 first-quarter points per game (T-4th) and allows 0.9 (1st) defensively. Utah has gassed up opponents early and carried a lead late; that’s been their M.O. Utah is on the nation’s longest winning streak, 14 games, after thrashing Cincinnati 49-25. The last loss came against BYU 24-21 last season. Utah can get revenge and, in the same breath, claim control of their destiny and the Big 12. If BYU loses to Utah, the Cougars’ college football hopes will rely on winning the Big 12 Championship. With a loss to UCF, BYU put their season on thin ice as Utah, BYU, and Texas Tech battle for the top two spots. BYU had a strong first half against Arizona State last week, leading 17-3 at the break, but was outscored 17-10 in the second half. BYU could get a boost this week with star running back and 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martin returning. Martin has missed the last four games and put a lot of the offensive pressure on Bear Bachmeier . While reports say Martin won’t be 100 percent if he plays, at least he could be a decoy that sets up Bachmeier in RPO or the downfield pass game. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. The Utes had 27 first downs, converted 7-of-11 third downs, posted 534 yards of offense, and averaged 6.4 yards per carry. Utah scored a ridiculous 42 points in the first half and led 42-6 at the half. The Utes scored on all four of their offensive drives in the first half, and the defense recorded a pick-six and fumble return for a touchdown. The Utes didn’t score on the first four drives of the second half, but it didn’t make much of a difference; the damage was already done to the Bearcats. Utah enters hot and ready for a shootout at 10 AM their time! Utah Player to Watch on Offense: QB Devon Dampier For the third time in the last four games, Devon Dampier threw three touchdown passes and 200-plus yards in seven straight. Dampier’s been on fire, and even when he’s not slinging touchdowns, he’s running for them. Dampier had 150 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Houston, then turned around and threw for three scores on Cincinnati. In the last four games, Dampier has 12 total touchdowns to one interception and averaged 309.5 total yards in that span, with Utah scoring 34.5 points per game. The Utes have been a tank, and if they win this game, Dampier can jump into the top five odds for the Heisman. The Utah Utes Defense: Utah’s defense has been one of my favorite units to watch this season. They fly around and lay the boom on opponents from the opening drive. Utah allowed over 200 yards in the first half, but Cincinnati couldn’t convert in the red zone, nor on the money downs. Cincinnati went 3-of-13 on third and fourth downs and only managed a 24:30 time of possession. It was a dominant performance from Utah, and in the first quarter, they’ve been the best team all season. Utah’s defense has allowed six total first-quarter points all season and a 0.9 first-quarter points-per-game average, which leads the country. Getting off to a quick start seems impossible for opponents this season; let’s see what BYU can do. Utah Player to Watch on Defense: DB Jackson Bennee In Utah’s biggest game of the season, Jackson Bennee posted a season-high eight tackles, had a sack, forced and recovered a fumble against Houston, then recorded four tackles against Cincinnati the following week. Bennee ranks third on the Utes with 36 tackles, third in pass deflections (4), and tied for the team lead in interceptions (2). Bennee led the team in picks last year (4) and was second in tackles (63), so he’s off to another strong season. BYU has at least stayed consistent with scoring: 24, 28, 31, and 27 points during that span. However, the rushing yardage has decreased each game and has lost the turnover battle 6-2 in that span, with at least one turnover in every game. Bear Bachmeier rose to Heisman candidacy after beating Notre Dame with four touchdowns, but after the loss to UCF and a seven-point win over Arizona State, he’s on the outside looking in. A win at Utah would help his case in a weekend where the Heisman Trophy race will have major chaos. BYU ranks 42th in passing grades per PFF and Utah is 47th in coverage grades, so that will be the biggest battle, outside of these massive offensive lines clashing in the trenches. BYU Player to Watch on Offense: RB LJ Martin LJ Martin has missed the last four games, and in that span, BYU has run for 177, 121, 116, and 47 rushing yards without Martin. Last season, Martin ran for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns, plus added 255 receiving yards on 35 catches. Martin was hurt against TCU, and the game prior, he posted a season-high 176 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Colorado State. Whether he is or is not 100 percent, Martin can be utilized in the red zone and short-yardage situations, plus the senior would be a great decoy for play-action early. The BYU Cougars Defense: BYU’s defense had one of its best first-half showings of the season against Arizona State. The Cougars held the Sun Devils to 107 yards and three points in the first half, but the second half was a different story. BYU gave up two straight touchdown drives of 12 and 13 plays for 81 and 39 yards. After that, a punt and field goal pulled the game within seven. BYU played the second half very conservatively in order to hold onto the win and come out healthy. BYU had six sacks, 8 TFL, and forced two fumbles. It was a bounce-back performance, to say the least, after allowing 463 yards to UCF and a season-high 39. Uluave had seven tackles and a sack against Arizona State last week after 10 tackles in the loss to UCF. Uluave led Cal last year with 97 tackles, was second in sacks (3.5), and fourth in pass deflections (4). Uluave has been a four-year starter in college and is an Utah native (South Jordan, UT). This will be a memorable game for Uluave; playing in his first and only Holy War. Jeremy Mauss BYU Cougars Wire Nov. 7, 2026, 9:16 a.m. CT BYU running back LJ Martin is set to return against No. 3 ranked Utah after being sidelined with an ankle injury since October 3. We’ll just keep looking at him throughout the week.” Even if Martin can’t go, the Cougars (7-1, 4-1 Big 12) aren’t running away from the issues. They’re not even placing the burden of fixing those problems on backup running backs like Sione Moa — who recently returned from a second leg injury in the past year — or Preston Rex, who saw a noticeable uptick in carries against Iowa State and Notre Dame before sitting out against Arizona State. The offensive line is certainly feeling it, starting with position coach TJ Woods. The outspoken run-game coordinator has been blunt with his players in meetings, during film review, and in practice as BYU works to figure out its rushing ahead of Saturday’s rivalry game at third-ranked, undefeated Utah (10 a.m. MT, ABC). “One thing coach Woods does a great job of is keeping us accountable,” said veteran guard Sonny Makasini, the fifth-year senior out of Timpview High. “Whether it’s a good game or a bad game, he’s going to let us know what we messed up on. The Cougars needed just 4.03 yards per carry to stun then-No. 2 Notre Dame, getting a career game from the converted safety Rex with 66 yards on 10 carries. But one week later, the average dropped to 3.22 yards per rush in a double-overtime loss at UCF and bottomed out at 47 total rush yards and just 1.6 yards per carry in Saturday’s 27-20 win over the Sun Devils. Clearly, figuring out the run game has been a topic of conversation in the offensive line group chat. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Two former Big 12 foes are set to clash for the first time as members of the SEC on Saturday Getty Images No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri will square off as SEC foes for the first time on Saturday in a clash between two-loss teams seeking traction in the College Football Playoff picture. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Where to watch Texas vs. Missouri live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Faurot Field -- Columbia, Missouri TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Texas vs. Missouri prediction, picks The best unit on this field is the Texas defense. Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. Staff Picks and Scores Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB After getting to play their entire October slate in the Lone Star State, the Longhorns are once again leaving town for Columbia, Missouri, to take on the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Texas 27, Missouri 20 Phoenix Haigis Texas has started to find their groove again with two major wins at home against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. The Longhorns now go back on the road against another ranked opponent in Missouri. As much momentum as Texas has going into this game, all the advantages matchup-wise go in favor of the Tigers. Texas is dealing with a significant amount of major injuries with the addition of running back Hollywood Smothers being out for the season while Missouri will see their running back Ahmad Hardy return for the first time this season. The Tigers are one of the best teams at home this year and have the best turnover margin in the SEC against a Lorghorns team that has had turnover issues this season. Although Texas is favored, the math tells a different story and could eliminate the Longhorns’ playoff chances. Zion Trammell Texas and Missouri have the makings of a defensive slugfest. It’ll be a cold morning in Columbia, Missouri, which could challenge the offenses. Both the Longhorns and Tigers rank in the top four in the SEC in average rushing yards allowed per game. Texas may need a big defensive play to win. I think Will Muschamp’s defense will deliver, and the Longhorns will win a close game on Saturday. Texas 21, Missouri 17 Oct 24, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Mississippi Rebels wide receiver Traylon Ray reacts after an incomplete pass defended by Texas Longhorns defensive back Jelani McDonald during the second half at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JD Andress Texas has multiple injuries to deal, and potentially more that could not fall off the injury report come game day. However, this feels like the Arch legacy game that many have been begging to see. Perhaps it's also because that might be what HAS to happen, but I'm riding with believing in Manning in this one. Oct 31, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles reacts after making a defensive stop during the second half against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Leo Barnes All things considered, I still like this Texas team. This will be a defensive dogfight. It won't be pretty, and it might even be a little boring at times — that is, if all you care about is high-flying action. And while the injury report isn't promising one bit, I still believe this Texas defense can be every bit as legitimate as it's proven itself to be. Stopping Missouri starts with shutting down the run game, and I fully expect Justin Cryer and Rasheem Biles to help answer the call. I could easily see either one leading the team in tackles by the time it's all said and done. Ultimately, Texas' ability to stonewall opposing offenses should be enough to keep the Tigers in check, giving its sometimes-average offense just enough breathing room to squeak out another win. He is also a senior sports reporter for The Daily Texan, where he currently covers the men’s basketball beat. Born and raised in Austin, Barnes roots for all things Texas, as well as the San Antonio Spurs and Dallas Cowboys. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Missouri Upset That Could Shake Texas' Playoff Hopes Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy believes Texas’ turnover problems will catch up with the Longhorns at Missouri, making the Tigers his lone outright upset pick of Week 10 as both 6-2 SEC teams fight to stay in the College Football Playoff race. McElroy backed the Tigers on his Always College Football podcast, predicting a low-scoring game decided by ball security. “The team that gives it away just one time, that’s the team that’s going to lose,” he said. Why is Greg McElroy picking Missouri? Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” The Tigers turned four Arkansas turnovers into 24 points in last week’s win in Fayetteville, and Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said afterward that “turnovers are the name of the game .” McElroy added that Missouri has scored 62 points off takeaways this season without allowing a point off a giveaway. “So when his team wins the turnover battle by one or more, Eli Drinkwitz is 39-4,” McElroy said. Texas checked in at No. 7 in the first College Football Playoff rankings , 11 spots ahead of Missouri. Still, both Missouri losses came on the road against Mississippi State and Ole Miss, two teams Texas beat over the last two weeks. Arch Manning’s costly turnover trouble Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on after a medical check during the game against Ole Miss | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Mississippi State sacked the redshirt junior six times last Saturday, and Texas now plays without left tackle Trevor Goosby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury against Ole Miss. “They average getting sacked nearly one out of every 10 dropbacks,” McElroy said of Texas. “That’s 126th because the breakdowns come from all over the protection.” The ESPN analyst said Texas has struggled when its receivers have to beat man coverage snap after snap, and he called Missouri’s cornerbacks “about as good as you find when it comes to playing that coverage week in and week out.” How does Texas reach 24 points? Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian celebrates with fans and players after the game against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” The Longhorns’ running game offers little relief, with McElroy saying their backs “are getting hit almost as soon as they take the handoff.” Running back Hollywood Smothers is out, and receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both listed as questionable on Thursday’s SEC availability report . Wingo, a St. Louis native Missouri recruited out of high school, leads Texas with 36 catches for 470 yards, while Coleman, an Auburn transfer, leads the team with seven touchdown catches. McElroy’s route to 24 points runs through Wingo “in the catch-and-run game” against a Missouri defense he said sits “at or near the bottom as far as missed tackles,” plus “one Coleman shot over the top.” “But without it, Texas might be living on field goals, which is a dangerous recipe on the road,” McElroy said. A loss would send Texas to LSU next week with three defeats, a scenario ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said could cause the Longhorns to “ collapse .” Texas visits Missouri at noon ET Saturday on ESPN. Arch Manning, Austin Simmons NCAAF Texas heads to Columbia with its top two receivers questionable, adding another concern for an offense that's struggled to find its rhythm. My Texas vs. Missouri prediction examines whether the Longhorns can overcome those issues against a dangerous Tigers defense. Missouri is a perfect 4-0 at home and fresh off a convincing 34-10 win at Arkansas. The Tigers know how to get after the quarterback, which could spell trouble for Arch Manning behind a shaky Texas offensive line. I'm taking the points with Missouri and expecting a low-scoring battle in Saturday's SEC showdown. Find out why in my latest college football picks for Week 10. TOP PICK Who will win Texas vs. Missouri: Missouri +2.5 I would play the Missouri Tigers to cover this number down to 52%. The Texas Longhorns ' passing game runs through Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo, and both are questionable after leaving the win over Mississippi State hurt. Coleman hasn't practiced this week. To make matters worse, left tackle Trevor Goosby is out. Arch Manning was already producing -0.04 EPA per dropback with all three of them in the lineup. Missouri's Austin Simmons sits at 0.20 EPA per dropback , and he gets a Texas secondary with two starting corners listed as questionable. Mizzou is 4-0 at home this season, winning those games by an average of 24.8 points. I'll gladly take the team in better form with the better offense. Texas vs. Missouri Over/Under pick: Under 43.5 I'd play the Under to 42.5. Missouri will want to lean on Jamal Roberts, but they own a 37.8% rushing success rate, 128th nationally . That's a rough matchup against a Texas defense allowing a 35.8% rushing success rate, seventh in the country. Missouri also stalls near the goal line, posting a 35.7% success rate in the red zone, 125th nationally . The Texas offense will come into this one banged up and already struggling. Neither offense is built to win a shootout. Texas vs. Missouri prop: Texas team total Under 23.5 Texas has posted negative offensive EPA per play in five straight games , and Coleman and Wingo were healthy for most of that stretch. Field position makes it worse. Texas ranks 137th of 138 teams in EPA per play on its own half of the field, so drives that start deep rarely flip the field. Missouri's defense ranks 11th in havoc rate at 19.1%, while Texas allows havoc on 17.1% of its snaps, 105th nationally. With Goosby out at left tackle, I don't see that gap closing. Texas vs. Missouri combo Every leg runs through the same idea. Texas' offense was already the weak link before its top receivers got hurt, and Missouri can win a low-scoring game at home. The moneyline anchors it. If Texas can't move the ball past midfield, Missouri doesn't need a big day from its own offense to win, and both totals stay low. If the Tigers' run game gets stuffed instead, that only strengthens the Under. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. Texas vs Missouri Odds, Point Spread, Betting Lines Texas vs Missouri Spread : Texas -2.5, Missouri +2.5 Texas vs Missouri Over/Under : 43.5 Total Points Texas vs Missouri Moneyline : Texas ML -135, Missouri ML +114 Even in a win over Mississippi State , the celebrations for Texas were cut short with Cam Coleman , Ryan Wingo and Hollywood Smothers all going down with injuries against the Bulldogs. That was a devastating result after Trevor Goosby — a pillar of the Longhorns' offensive line who is projected to be a top-10 pick in next year's draft — had already been ruled out for the remainder of the year. The injuries for Texas could be the straw that breaks the camel's back, with the Longhorns already struggling on offense, limping into Week 10 ranked 74th in Success Rate, 95th in Explosiveness and 129th in Havoc Allowed. Arch Manning's inconsistencies have made it difficult for Texas to stay ahead of the sticks, leaving the offense vulnerable to stalling out early on in drives. While Coleman and Wingo are expected to play at less than 100%, Smothers' outlook looks bleak, forcing the Longhorns to lean more heavily on Raleek Brown . When given the opportunity, Brown has been a consistent source of production in the Texas backfield, averaging nearly five yards per carry. With question marks lingering over the offense, the Longhorns will need to continue to play at a high level on the other side of the ball in order to keep their hopes of making the playoffs alive. Luckily for Texas, the defense has been the strength of the team this season, entering Week 10 ranked in the top 25 in Success Rate, Explosiveness, Finishing Drives and Havoc. Missouri 's hot start to the year is arguably one of the bigger surprises of the season, with the Tigers just one win away from clearing the over on their regular-season win total while sitting 1.5 games back from first in the SEC conference standings. Austin Simmons ' resurgence under center has played a major role in Missouri's success, throwing just two interceptions in eight games while averaging 8.1 yards per throw. While Simmons has been able to thrive through the air, the Tigers' running back room has yet to find its footing, ranking near the bottom of the board in Rush Success Rate and PPA. When Jamal Roberts is unable to hit the ground running, opposing defenses can stretch out their linebackers across the middle, smothering Simmons' passing lanes at multiple levels of the field. It is worth noting Ahmad Hardy was able to make his return to the field after suffering a scary gunshot wound in the offseason, potentially giving Missouri the spark it needs to be a well-rounded offense. While his return was welcome to see, expectations will need to be tempered, with the Tigers' running back being held to just two carries. Like Texas, Missouri has also built its success on the shoulders of the defense, fielding a group that ranks 29th in Success Rate and fifth in Havoc. While the Tigers do give up explosive plays at an alarming rate, they are able to successfully keep their opponents out of the end zone, giving up just 3.03 Points per Opportunity. While Simmons has been able to play far better than initially expected, negative regression is looming large over the Tigers' quarterback as he battles it out against a secondary that excels in coverage, per its top-30 mark in Dropback EPA Allowed per play. With the Longhorns keeping a body on Missouri's pass-catchers' hips, the amount of Havoc in Simmons' throws will increase, leading to an uptick in his total number of Turnover-Worthy Plays. Even with Hardy back on the field, it's tough to envision the star running back being able to quickly shake off the rust, making the Tigers far too one-dimensional. Barring a sudden turnaround on the ground, Texas will be able to drop more bodies back in coverage, making it easier to create disruptions. Colin Simmons has also been upgraded to questionable, yet it remains to be seen if the Longhorns' edge rusher will suit up on Saturday. While the Longhorns do generate pressure at a high rate, Simmons would help pull defensive attention to the edge, freeing up more space in the interior to help the middle of the defensive line collapse the pocket. With no clear path for success, expect Missouri to be held to early outs at a consistent rate, chipping away at the Tigers' total number of scoring opportunities. Place a wager on Missouri to be held under the team total of 20.5, with intentions of adding more to your position should the market tick back up to the key number of 21. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Missouri ranks just 12 th in the SEC with 11 sacks in league play, but the Longhorns have struggled to protect QB Arch Manning while allowing 20 sacks in five SEC games. If a revamped Texas line with two tackles in new positions in right tackle Andre Cojoe and left tackle Melvin Siani can give Manning time, he may exploit a Tiger defense that gives up 260.4 yards passing a game in league play. When Missouri has the ball The Tigers like to pound the ball, especially since Hardy made his season debut last week against Arkansas. If Hardy can find the form that helped him rush for 3,000 yards and 29 TDs over his first two collegiate seasons, he'll team with Roberts in arguably the best backfield in college football. But Texas gives up yards on the ground grudgingly; the defense allows just 98.4 yards per game rushing in SEC play, which ranks only behind Georgia. The secondary may be the most beat-up unit on the squad, which is saying something for the bruised and battered Longhorns. Graceson Littleton , an elite slot corner, will likely miss the game. So could starting cornerback Kade Phillips. Texas could compensate by moving top corner Bo Mascoe to the slot, which is a critical position for the Longhorns' defense that ranks 10 th in the nation with 273.1 yards allowed per game MORE: How tight ends, backs can help the worst passing game in the Sarkisian-era Texas vs Missouri key matchup Texas cornerback Warren Roberson vs. Missouri receiver Cayden Lee Veteran Warren Roberson, who has played in 36 career games for the Longhorns, could get his first career start for the Longhorns' banged-up corners. It's a daunting debut, since Missouri's Cayden Lee leads the SEC with 756 yards receiving on 53 catches. Texas vs Missouri prediction Thomas Jones: Missouri 23, Texas 20. Texas has a history of playing well in big games under head coach Steve Sarkisian, but can the Longhorns find the needed emotional spark in their first conference visit to this SEC hinterlands? It's the game of the year for many Mizzou fans; it feels like a trap for Texas. Danny Davis: Texas. The Longhorns are solidly back in the CFP conversation and will remain so even if the defense has to carry them to another win this weekend in Columbia as injuries and inefficiencies continue to haunt the UT offense. Cedric Golden: Texas 24, Missouri 21. The Longhorns are beaten up and understand how essential this win will be to their postseason hopes. They have a much better chance of beating Missouri than they do of winning at LSU next week. They take advantage and eek out a win, thanks again to the defense. Michael Shapiro: Texas 20, Missouri 19. Texas' defense will stiffen in the red zone against a strong Missouri run game, and Arch Manning will continue to churn yards on the ground in a grinding, just-effective-enough afternoon for the Longhorns' offense. This is life in the SEC. It might not be pretty, but every win is another point of evidence for Steve Sarkisian as he makes Texas' case for inclusion in the College Football Playoff. away.headline: Longhorns Injury Report: Status of Simmons, Smothers, Coleman updated
away.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Texas Longhorns have been bitten by the injury bug and there are some big names on the SEC availability report . Several key players were hurt in Texas' 31-3 win over Mississippi State. And while there have been rumors and reports , now we know who is out and who might play. We know offensive tackle Trevor Goosby is out for the season. Edge Richard Wesley has been out for weeks. Now, running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend are out for the game at Missouri. Smothers reportedly hurt his knee and shoulder against the Bulldogs. Townsend is a bit of a surprise. Wide receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both in street clothes on the sideline by the end of the game against Hail State. Both are listed as questionable. Defensive backs Kade Phillips and Graceson Littleton were also injured last Saturday night. They are also listed as questionable. All-American edge Colin Simmons is also listed as questionable. Arguably the best player on the team has missed two games with a high-ankle sprain. He was briefly listed as questionable last week, but was downgraded to out. We'll see what happens this week.
