away.headline: Texas's final injury report provides a slight reprieve for the Longhorns vs. Missouri
away.blurb: With one brutal injury list after another, it looked like the Horns could be without as many as eight or nine starters. Luckily, in Texas's final availability report ahead of kickoff, it looked like the Horns might actually catch a break as a few players shifted toward being available. On Friday night, defensive backs Kade Phillips and Graceson Littleton were both listed as "probable" after spending a majority of the week under the "questionable" category, as was wide receiver Ryan Wingo. However, as most injury reports go, it was not all good news for Texas. We have known for a couple of weeks that starting left tackle Trevor Goosby was out for the rest of the season, but starting running back Hollywood Smothers joined him on that list after tearing his MCL. Additionally, edge rusher Richard Wesley and tight end Nick Townsend were both on the availability report, once again, as "out." Then, star edge rusher Colin Simmons was listed as "questionable" for a third straight week after suffering a high-ankle sprain against the Florida Gators in Week 7. Wide receiver Cam Coleman joined Simmons in the grey area after getting beat up against Mississippi State last week. On ESPN's College GameDay , Pete Thamel reported that the two were "game-time decisions," with Simmons seeing a larger likelihood of suiting up and actually setting foot on the field. OUT: Trevor Goosby (OL), Hollywood Smothers (RB), Nick Townsend (TE), Richard Wesley (EDGE) QUESTIONABLE: Colin Simmons (EDGE), Cam Coleman (WR) PROBABLE: Ryan Wingo (WR), Kade Phillips (DB), Graceson Littleton (DB) While any injuries are far from ideal, the final availability report of the week was far from the worst news for the Longhorns. Yes, a few stars are still out or doubtful, but it also looked like quite a few would be available in the top-20 SEC matchup. OUT: Malae Fonoti (RB), Josh Atkins (OL), Gavin Hoffman (TE) Last week saw the return of Missouri's star running back Ahmad Hardy, who had suffered a gunshot wound to the leg this offseason. While he did not see many reps in Week 9, one could expect his workload to increase as the Tigers and the Longhorns clashed. No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri are scheduled to kick off at 11 a.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the game will be available on both ABC and fuboTV. With a win, the Horns could take one more step toward cementing their place in this season's College Football Playoff. Texas's final injury report provides a slight reprieve for the Longhorns vs. Missouri Skip to main content Recruiting Earlier this week, Texas head football coach Steve Sarkisian acknowledged just how "undermanned" the Longhorns could be against the Missouri Tigers. That is a huge relief for the Horns on both sides of the ball, returning the depth for Texas's defensive secondary and giving quarterback Arch Manning his No. 1 target in the receiving corps. home.blurb: Mizzou published its first of four SEC-mandated availability and injury reports on Wednesday, Nov. 4, ahead of its game this coming Saturday against Texas, and added no new names to begin the week. That marks the second straight week that the Tigers have opened a game week without any injury concerns beyond players previously ruled out for the year. The major injury news comes out of Austin, Texas, as the Longhorns listed multiple starters and key players with availability designations. On offense for Texas, starting wideouts Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo were listed as questionable, and rotational running back Hollywood Smothers has been ruled out. On defense for the Longhorns, star defensive end Colin Simmons is questionable. Starting nickel Graceson Littleton and cornerback Kade Phillips, who have played the fifth- and sixth-most defensive snaps for the Longhorns this season, respectively, also were questionable. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. EDG #1 Colin Simmons (Questionable) WR #1 Ryan Wingo (Questionable) WR #8 Cam Coleman (Questionable) DB #8 Kade Phillips (Questionable) DB #29 Graceson Littleton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. home.headline: Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri
home.blurb: Texas RB Hollywood Smothers Out for Rest of Season Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Story by Texas Longhorns On SI videos Texas Gets Devastating Hollywood Smothers Injury Update Ahead of Missouri Texas Longhorns running back Hollywood Smothers (2) warms up before a game against the Mississippi State Cougars at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zach Dimmitt · Texas Longhorns On SI videos Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:01 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Texas Longhorns have been no stranger to the injury bug this season, though this hasn't stopped the team from being firmly in the College Football Playoff race. Already without starting left tackle Trevor Goosby for the remainder of the season, the injury issues have piled up for Texas headed into Saturday's road matchup with the Missouri Tigers. Now, the Longhorns are receiving worst-case scenario news when it comes to starting running back Hollywood Smothers, who exited last week's game against Mississippi State with an apparent lower-body injury. Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. In the second half against Mississippi State, Smothers took a hard hit to his lower body and sat on the turf holding his left knee. He was then helped off the field by trainers and was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Smothers finishes his 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns along with 10 catches for 79 yards and another score. His pair of rushing touchdowns came in one of the biggest moments of Texas' season, as he had two scores in the fourth quarter against Ohio State, highlighted by the game-winning touchdown in the final minute to complete the comeback. The Longhorns have already gotten accustomed to life without Smothers this season. He previously dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries, forcing him to miss games against Tennessee and Ole Miss. Texas running back Raleek Brown now becomes the no-doubt starter moving forward for the Longhorns. So far this season, he's tallied 92 carries for 452 yards and five touchdowns along with 12 catches for 54 yard and another score. This was highlighted by an impressive performance in the win over Ole Miss when he had 23 carries for 157 yards. Behind him, Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper will continue to receive an uptick in snaps. Terry has impressed and appears to have overtaken Cooper on the depth chart. It feels likely Terry will be Brown's backup moving forward. No. 7 Texas and No. 18 Missouri will kickoff from Columbia on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT. The Bruins haven't played on the road since sneaking past Oregon for their best win on Oct. 10. The Bruins were No. 8 in the first round of College Football Playoff rankings, which doesn't matter. If they end up 10-2, as a Big Ten team, they're a mortal lock to get into the CFP. But at this point, they want a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and they're good enough to beat anyone left on the slate. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. It beat Iowa and Michigan, but a weird 41-13 loss at Purdue is an issue for an at-large CFP spot. However, win out, and there's a shot at getting into the Big Ten title game. UCLA vs Minnesota: Quick Hits UCLA gets Illinois in the Rose Bowl next, then has to travel to Michigan, and finishes up down the road at USC. Minnesota goes to Penn State next week, hosts Northwestern, and close with the Paul Bunyan Axe game at Wisconsin. The two programs have only faced each other four times, with Minnesota winning the last meeting 21-17 in 2024. The Gophers are 3-1, starting with a 21-3 win in the 19162 Rose Bowl. How To Watch UCLA vs Minnesota Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Huntington Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, MN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why UCLA Will Win Run, run, and keep running. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too. UCLA vs Minnesota Prediction, Betting Lines The whole Big Noon Kickoff aspect to this is a problem for UCLA. The Bruins have to be ready to rumble at 9:00 am Los Angeles time. And then there's the other issue. When the ball gets kicked off in Minneapolis, it will be around 71 degrees in LA. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. It'll be another tremendously entertaining Minnesota game to kick off a whale of a Saturday. It'll be an early kickoff for UCLA , with the game getting underway at 9:00a.m. Pacific Time but, meaning it'll be a test for the whole program to prepare the right way to be undaunted by the early game time. Ahead of the game though, UCLA announced that they will be without WR Mikey Matthews, QB Nico Iamaleava, DB Rodrick Pleasant, WR Jonah Smith, WR Jalen Saint Paul, DL Ashton Sanders, OL Sam Yoon, P Curtis Gerrand and OLB Ryan McCulloch. UCLA will be down some key contributors for Saturday's game but even with the shorthandedness, the Bruins remain favored in the game. As of Friday night, UCLA is four point favorites after opening the week as 6.5 point favorites. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots : When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State . Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Our Alabama vs. LSU prediction and college football picks back Lane Kiffin and the Tigers to snap their Saban Bowl losing streak as Alabama seeks its fourth straight series victory on the first Saturday in November. The Crimson Tide visit Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., where LSU enters as a 5. 5-point favorite in Death Valley. Kickoff is scheduled for 3: 30 p. m. ET on ABC on Saturday, Nov. 7. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). Alabama vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 52.5 This game isn't one of the must-watch games in my college football Top 25 predictions this week because I'm expecting offensive fireworks; it's because of the talent on these defenses. LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But I don't expect an offensive onslaught from LSU either. This is the best defense the Tigers have faced this season, with Alabama ranking 20th nationally in available yards percentage (37.7%) and 14th in net adjusted EPA per play. Alabama vs LSU prop: Alabama TT Under 23.5 Alabama's offense has no identity, and Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb don't seem to know how to fix it. The Crimson Tide have faced two high-quality defenses this season and failed to score more than 17 points in both games. Against LSU, I like the Under on the Crimson Tide's team total at 21.5 or better . Alabama continues to deal with two key injuries on the offensive side of the ball, with both center Racin Delgatty and wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams questionable for this game. If those two don't play, Alabama will struggle to score even 20 points. The Crimson Tide don't have consistent playmakers outside of Coleman-Williams, and LSU's defense brings the heat, ranking fourth nationally in havoc rate (22.2%) . Alabama vs LSU combo Alabama has gotten off to slow starts and failed to cover in three straight games as a result. In the Crimson Tide's last three games, it trailed Georgia 10-0, trailed Tennessee 9-0, and trailed Texas A&M 14-10. If Alabama gets off to another slow start and trails LSU, the Tigers' defense will pin their ears back and go to work. LSU ranks eighth nationally in pass success rate on defense (36%) and has one of the most lethal pass rush duos in the country, Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross (58 combined pressures and 13.5 sacks). Death Valley is one of the hardest places to play, and with Alabama's broken offense, I don't expect the Tide to score much early against this opportunistic LSU defense. Both Alabama and LSU come into the game with a record of 6-2, giving each team a chance to make a real statement . Each team is coming off a bye week, giving them more rest and time to prepare for this huge game. With SEC schedule changes coming, this matchup will be the last one played between the two teams on a yearly basis. This could add more emphasis for both sides to want to come away with the win. With this rivalry game kicking off in a few days, the Crimson Tide aren't being favored to come away with the win on the road. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Alabama only has a 43 percent chance of taking down LSU this week. Since the game is being played on the road, LSU is likely being favored, especially since Tiger Stadium can be so tough to play in. One of the bigger keys to the game for the Crimson Tide will be how quarterback Keelon Russell can perform. Alabama has all the confidence in the world in Russell, but he has been a little shaky at times this season. For the year, the signal-caller has thrown for 2,057 yards with 15 touchdowns and five interceptions through the air. On the ground, Russell has made his presence known for this team, rushing for Russell has proven to be very impactful for Alabama, even with his limited experience as a starting quarterback. If Russell can handle the hostile atmosphere that LSU will throw at him, the Crimson Tide could have a strong chance to win the game. Alabama is going to need Russell to play more like he did against Kentucky earlier in the season, rather than how he looked against Tennessee a few weeks ago. The signal-caller have a lot of talent, but he can sometimes make poor decisions with the football. LSU has a very strong defense, and this will be a major challenge for Russell to overcome this week. But if Alabama is going to reach the heights that this program wants to get to this season, Russell is going to have to be able to handle these types of games. Kickoff for the final yearly meeting between the two rivals is set for 12:30 p.m. PT/3:30 p.m. ET from Baton Rouge.

It's possible that the loser of this game could still get into the playoff with three losses — it depends on how the rest of the season plays out — but the winner will be the only one that controls its own destiny moving forward. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his score prediction for the game, and he has LSU leaving Tiger Stadium with a 27-20 win. With both teams 6-2 this season, the final stretch of the season, starting this Saturday, will show who's the best playoff contender . The staff of LSU Tigers on SI has made their picks for the LSU vs. Alabama game. LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin walks on the sideline during the first quarter against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect College Football Playoff hopes will be on the line Saturday. LSU and Alabama would love to notch a signature win. Alabama's opportunistic secondary could trouble Sam Leavitt and the offense. If Leavitt protects the ball and the defensive line takes advantage of a potentially vulnerable Crimson Tide offensive line, LSU should win. Tiger Stadium will be deafening, and I think the Tigers will make a statement on Saturday. LSU 35, Alabama 24 I think that the Tigers win a close one at home. This freshly healthy Alabama squad will be a tough challenge for these LSU Tigers, but I think that the LSU defense will come up with a pick-six late in the game to seal their victory. LSU 31, Alabama 28 LSU and Lane Kiffin are ready to take down Alabama. For Kiffin, he's 0-5. For LSU, a three-year losing streak will end. Sam Leavitt has made the jump and taken care of the football and looked sharp through the air, with LSU having solid o-line play to lead the way in establishing the run and attacking Alabama's defense in every way. The Tigers' defense is ready for the challenge too. With Alabama missing some key pieces on the o-line, and LSU's dominant pass rush, the matchup easily favors the Tigers. LSU 45, Alabama 21 Brooke Benedict LSU and Alabama have shown a similar weakness this season, as both teams reveal critical system errors and momentum failures when trailing in a game. Alabama showed this against Tennessee and LSU has shown this against Ole Miss, both major opponents this season. As Saturday's matchup brings the same level of competition, it's key that both teams don't let the score turn lopsided. With the home-field advantage, I think LSU will be able to gain the momentum early, and Alabama will lose key momentum in the environment of Tiger Stadium. LSU 28, Alabama 20 While LSU vs. Alabama isn't a "storied" rivalry, it's perhaps some of the best football that gets played each year, and this matchup will be no different. Kiffin is looking for his first signature win with LSU, and if Sam Leavitt continues to play the same way he has the last two weeks, I expect it to happen. LSU 38, Alabama 30 Hannah Garcia I think that LSU is going to pull out the victory this weekend just because, for one thing, Alabama is missing their top receiver, Ryan Coleman Williams. Despite the fact that they have a really good quarterback in Keon Russell, I do think that the vital piece of their offense being missing will affect their game this weekend. I also think that our defense is a lot stronger than theirs is; we are holding opponents to fewer points per game than their team is, despite both defenses being really good. In terms of our offense, I think that Sam Levitt has been on the up and up the past couple of games; he hasn't thrown any interceptions, and he's looking more like the 2024 CFP quarterback that he once was. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joshua Chatham · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:18 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Happy Friday, everyone. The women's basketball team feasted on yet another cupcake last night to move to 3-0, this time taking down Alabama A&M by a 96-43 margin . The men play tonight against Arkansas State, and we will have coverage of that one later on. Alabama football plays at LSU tomorrow, as you well know. Your previews: Alabama gets an immediate chance to justify its CFP ranking, while LSU can strengthen its argument with a win that leaves the Tide staring at three losses. I picked LSU to win this game in August, and I'm sticking with the Tigers' passing game at home against an Alabama secondary still sorting through injuries. Sam Leavitt throws for 278 yards and two touchdowns, and Jackson Harris catches both of them while finishing with 110 receiving yards. LSU wins 26-20, keeping its SEC title hopes alive and giving Alabama fans another reason to avoid the internet. Alabama football needs this win. Kalen DeBoer wins after idle weeks. And the Crimson Tide knows how to win against LSU on the road. All of these remain true. But this is a new Tigers team in a new era with Lane Kiffin at the helm. It's a unit starting to find itself after single-score losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky. LSU has the second best scoring offense and defense in the SEC. It has the No. 1 total offense and defense in the SEC. This is a Tigers team that is waiting for an opportunity to see what it can do against the upper echelon of SEC play in November, and the Crimson Tide is the first team in LSU's way. Alabama has looked like the best team in the country before on the road, beating Mississippi State to a pulp in Starkville, but the same couldn't be said about Kentucky in Lexington, or, especially, Tennessee in Knoxville. Expect the Crimson Tide to falter against LSU. Prediction: No. 15 LSU 31, No. 9 Alabama 24 While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. LSU is a completely different animal in Baton Rouge. It's an afternoon game instead of an ultra-amped up night showdown in Death Valley, but it shouldn't matter too much that the Tiger fan base is just a little less … prepared. Yeah, Ole Miss, Kentucky, and Auburn are, arguably, the three best teams LSU faced, which is why those road games were tough, but LSU hasn't even let the opponents breathe at home, winning all five games by a combined score of 225-44 with the closest game a 35-6 win over Texas A&M. LSU won't destroy Alabama, and it'll be a back-and-forth fight, but there will be that moment in the second half when it all clicks, and the Tigers will put the game away with a sharp scoring drive. The crowd will take over from there. LSU 30, Alabama 23 John Brice: LSU Matt Hayes: LSU Jordan Mendoza: Alabama Paul Myerberg: LSU Erick Smith: Alabama Eddie Timanus: LSU Blake Toppmeyer: LSU Craig Meyer: Alabama 31, LSU 27 LSU 35, Alabama 28: Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt was flat out bad in his first three games: He threw three touchdowns and five interceptions against Clemson, Louisiana Tech and Ole Miss. Since then, he has completed 75.4% of his passes and has vastly reduced his turnovers as he's adjusted to coach Lane Kiffin's system. Keelon Russell can get just as hot for the Crimson Tide. We just haven't seen as much of that lately, so we'll lean toward Leavitt and Co. here. — Adam Bittner, USA TODAY This LSU team continues to impress. They now enter Week 10 ranking first in the entire country in net adjusted EPA per play, seventh in net yards per play, and seventh in net success rate. That's a step above Alabama, which ranks fifth, 15th, and ninth in those three metrics. The one weakness that LSU has is stopping the run, ranking just 54th in opponent EPA per rush, but unfortunately for the Crimson Tide, they haven't run the ball efficiently this season, ranking just 50th in EPA per rush. Without the ability to take advantage of LSU's biggest weakness, this is going to be a tough road game for Alabama. I'll lay the points with the Tigers. The sportsbooks have LSU laying nearly a touchdown at home against Alabama. That means at a neutral site, LSU would be favored by roughly a field goal, so Las Vegas believes the Tigers are the better team. While LSU has played better of late, and I would anticipate Lane Kiffin dialing up some trickeration in this game, LSU hasn't beaten Alabama since 2022 and Kiffin historically has struggled against the Tide. Give me Alabama to win a close one inside Tiger Stadium Saturday. Alabama 24, LSU 21 That last one is from The Daily Advertiser. We see what you're trying to pull, bro. There is no reason whatsoever for Alabama fans to have much confidence in this one. We have a third of the starting lineup listed as questionable, and we saw what happened in Knoxville when none of those guys played. Word is that Alabama expects to get some key players back, but will they be 100%? On top of that, Keelon Russell has struggled at times against the blitz this season, and will be facing one of the most blitz-happy teams in the country. It does appear that LSU will be without MLB Whit Weeks, so that will help. Still, this is perhaps the most hostile environment in the sport, against a team that leads the SEC in both offense and defense, that also happens to need this win to get into the playoff discussion after Tuesday night's rankings dropped. Sure, they are in this position because they lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky, but those were road games. Still, we Gump to a standard around here. The one thing that Alabama can point to is Sam Leavitt's propensity to turn the ball over, and Alabama's defense has been as opportunistic as any in the country. We're going to say that the bye week afforded Russell the opportunity to learn from film study, and Alabama will get just enough guys back to get it done in Red Stick as they have so many times in the past. Leavitt has two picks, including one returned for a touchdown, and Alabama wins 30-27. That is merely my hopium, of course. Let us know your thoughts in the comments. Matt Stahl correctly notes that Alabama needs explosive plays in the passing game to win this one. Ryan Coleman-Williams is on the road to recovery, but was still listed as questionable for LSU after missing the Tennessee and Texas A&M games. Tiger head coach Lane Kiffin predicted Thursday that the junior wideout will play, but that isn't guaranteed. Coleman-Williams can provide an explosive play threat whenever he's on the field. Against Tennessee, that lack of explosives was obvious, and contributed to the loss. That same thing can't happen in Tiger Stadium. Even if its superstar receiver can't go, Alabama has to find some big plays on offense. Lotzeir Brooks is a threat, as is Rico Scott. The Crimson Tide could also find explosives from the likes of Derek Meadows and Cederian Morgan at receiver. There always needs to be a semblance of balance, but this is not a "run the ball" game. LSU leads the SEC in rushing defense, allowing only 2.7 yards per carry and 85 yards per contest. In order to push the ball down the field, Alabama's tackles will have to neutralize DE Princewill Umanmielen. Alabama has faced some prominent pass-rushers this season, but LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen has a strong argument to be the best. Umanmielen's 8.5 sacks rank fifth in the country, while his 12 tackles for loss are tied for ninth. The senior is second in the SEC in each of these stat categories. There have been numerous instances this season where Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell has held the ball for too long, and giving any edge to Umanmielen, along with the rest of LSU's pass-rush — which leads the country in sacks per game (4.4) — will make it very difficult for Alabama to come out on top. None of this will be easy. That's about it for today. Have a great weekend.

away.blurb: Alabama (7-2, 5-2) played like its season depended on it, jumping out to a first-half lead and overpowering the Tigers in their own home for a 31-13 victory. Freshman quarterback Kaelon Russell put on a show, throwing for 206 yards and three touchdowns, picking LSU’s defense apart when it matter most. Despite being outgained in total yards of offense, the Crimson Tide made the most of every red zone trip they had, while the same couldn’t be said for Lane Kiffin and his Tigers. LSU ended the game going 2 out of 4 in its red zone visits, with both of those red zone trips ending in field goals instead of touchdowns. With this loss, LSU falls to .500 in conference play and possibly out of playoff contention. Kiffin and the Tigers will look to flush this one quickly with No. 10 Texas coming to town on Nov. 14. The story of this game will come down to which quarterback can perform better. Sam Leavitt has been better for the Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) of late. His las time out at Auburn, he threw for 387 yards, accounted for four touchdowns but arguably more important, he didn't have a turnover. After a 32-yard punt return from Coleman-Williams, Russell only needed one play to extend Alabama's lead in the fourth quarter. The freshman signal caller dropped a dime from 25 yards out to wide receiver Cederian Morgan for a touchdown. The play only took five second off the clock, a good thing for LSU who now has even more of a hill to climb to make a comeback. LSU's defense was never in position on that drive and got burned twice. That's one of the few times all season Blake Baker's defense looked befuddled and out of place. Leavitt and company came out of the halftime looking to put points on the board. While they still have yet to taste the endzone, Leavitt and running back Dillin Jones were able to get the Tigers back in scoring position on their opening second-half drive. Staryzk capped the drive off with a 41-yard field goal to make it a four-point game. LSU football stalling out in the red zone Crimson Tide is running the ball today, something I thought would rougher for it to do against LSU. Alabama is winning one of the one-on-one battles when LSU's defense is out there right now. LSU faced a fourth and long to start the second quarter and elected to trust in Staryzk's foot to give it the lead. Staryzk attempted a field goal from 56 yards out and pushed it far left for his first miss of the day. With both the Tigers (6-3, 3-3 SEC) and Crimson Tide entering the matchup with two losses, losing on Saturday Nov. 7, inside Tiger Stadium wasn’t an option if either team wanted to solidify themselves as a possible College Football Playoff team. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. away.headline: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon
away.blurb: Timmons, who was held out of last week’s loss at USC with an unspecified injury, was not included on the Buckeyes’ initial availability report released for their upcoming game against the Ducks. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland earlier in October before returning at Indiana when he reaggravated his injury. He traveled with the Buckeyes to Los Angeles last week as he attempted to return but was ruled out near kickoff. Wide receivers Brock Boyd and Brandon Inniss were listed as questionable for Oregon after they were held out at USC. It was the second straight game Boyd was sidelined with an unspecified injury. Left tackle Ian Moore was also listed as questionable. Moore made a late exit against the Trojans as Austin Siereveld moved over from right tackle to replace him in the fourth quarter. Defensive tackle Eddrick Houston was not listed after he went down late last week and later limped off the field at the Coliseum, indicating he could be available against Oregon. He has also practiced in recent days, prompting coach Ryan Day to express optimism about his status on Nov. 4. “We’ll have to see how the next 48 hours go,” Day said, “but he’s had two good days of practice. That would really inject a lot for us in the back end.” The Buckeyes’ secondary felt the absence of Timmons against the Trojans as they surrendered their longest passes this season between a 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage and another 70-yard reception in the third quarter. Kentucky are ranked as high as it ever has, while the 6-2 Volunteers had their CFP hopes take a hit last week with a 27-24 loss at South Carolina . But there will be a sea of orange in Knoxville to welcome the upstarts. Saturday's kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET. The Volunteers are 6-point home favorites at DraftKings, and the Over/Under for total points scored is 49.5. Kentucky vs. Tennessee betting odds (via DraftKings) Kentucky vs. Tennessee money line: Kentucky +170, Tennessee -205 Kentucky vs. Tennessee Over/Under: 49.5 (Over -108, Under -112) Kentucky vs. Tennessee spread: Kentucky vs. Tennessee betting preview The Wildcats have won six in a row since a 45-17 loss to Alabama the second week of the season. Now they will face Tennessee, Florida and Missouri in successive weeks, so Stein's crew will need to be on top of its game. UK already has victories over ranked Texas A&M and LSU squads. It comes in off an easy 34-27 victory against Vanderbilt and had a bye last week, so it should be ready for this one. The Wildcats put up 376 yards last week, including 173 on the ground, and allowed 247. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has been avoiding mistakes as UK relies on running backs CJ Baxter , Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. Minchey is completing 69% of his passes for 1,755 yards, 14 TDs and just one interception. He also has two rushing scores, but the running back trio is the bread and butter. All three backs average more than 5 yards per carry, with Baxter the bell cow, as he has 487 rushing yards and eight TDs. Patterson has 443 yards and three scores and Barnes has 224 and a TD on 43 carries. Baxter and Patterson each have runs of more than 70 yards. Both teams average more than 32 points per game and Tennessee is eighth in the SEC in total yardage (394.5 ypg) while UK is ninth (386.4). The Vols are much better defensively, ranking fourth in the conference in yards allowed (288.4 ypg) and third in scoring (16.3 ppg). The Wildcats are allowing 24.8 points (10th in SEC) and 362.6 yards per game (11th). Where Kentucky has a big edge is in turnover margin, as the Wildcats are plus-13, fourth-best in the nation, while the Vols are plus-3. The Volunteers are strong defensively, and their offense also relies heavily on the run game. Only South Carolina averages more rushing yards than the Vols' 213 yards per game among conference foes, while UK averages 167 per contest on the ground, seventh in the conference. Running back DeSean Bishop is sixth in the nation with 957 rushing yards and has four consecutive games over 100, including 220 against Auburn . He has also scored 11 touchdowns. Backup Daune Morris has 349 yards and two scores, and he and Bishop both average more than 5.5 yards per carry. Quarterback George MacIntyre has played in place of Faizon Brandon the past four games, but he has two TD passes and five interceptions over that span. He also made a costly mistake against the Gamecocks last week. He did have some big plays nullified and is completing 67% of his passes compared to Brandon's 60%, but the latter has accounted for 10 TDs. Brandon has just one interception but has been sacked 15 times. Both could see time, but Brandon has dealt with a shoulder injury and MacIntyre has been up and down, so the running game and defense will be the keys. The Vols lead FBS in sacks with 35, led by Tyree Weathersby's seven, which ties him for ninth in the nation. Xavier Gilliam has six and Mariyon Dye has five as they're among nine players with at least two. The Vols have turned the ball over a lot but have 14 takeaways, tied for 14th in FBS. The Wildcats are tied for fourth in the nation with 18. The hosts will be looking to make up for last week, when they rushed for 184 yards but MacIntyre fumbled on a strip sack with 33 seconds left to set up the winning field goal. He threw for 136 yards. The Vols had five sacks of LaNorris Sellers and controlled the ball but couldn't hold off the South Carolina rally. Kentucky has covered the spread in every game except the loss to Alabama, and its games have gone Over the total in five of eight, including two of three on the road. Six of eight Vols games have gone Under, with all five home games falling short of the total. They are 4-4 against the spread and 3-2 ATS in Knoxville. Tennessee has won 12 of the past 14 meetings (one win was vacated), including 56-34 last October in Lexington. The running games should dominate, so the clock will be running, and neither quarterback is much of a threat to start loading up the stat sheet. The defenses allow just over 45 points between them, while the offenses combine for more than 65. The Wildcats battled to a 21-17 victory against a comparable defense in Oklahoma , which is fifth in the SEC in total defense. The Vols also play a lot of lower-scoring games at home, and the defense is going to be riled up. The SportsLine model has the Vols winning 67% of the time and covering at a 53% rate, but its best play is on the total. It has a 'B' grade on Under 50.5 , which hits 59.8% of the time. The projected final score is 27-19. SportsLine expert Eric Cohen agrees, as he is backing the Under. "With an uncertain quarterback situation, it does not benefit Josh Heupel's team to get into a shootout," he says, and he is predicting a 20-14 Tennessee victory. One major reason for the Wildcats' rise was Ohio State's loss to USC on Saturday. Kentucky is now 7-1 overall and 5-1 in SEC play, making the Wildcats one of the most surprising teams in college football this season, especially under first-year head coach Will Stein. The last time Kentucky took the field, the Wildcats defeated Vanderbilt 34-17 at home. However, they got off to a slow start, falling behind 10-0 before turning things around and taking the lead into halftime. Kentucky eventually took care of business to secure another SEC victory. Now, the Wildcats will hit the road to Knoxville this weekend to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Kentucky's most recent road game came against Oklahoma, where the Wildcats escaped Norman with a 21-13 victory. Kentucky will look to replicate that performance against Tennessee, but the Volunteers' defense has been one of the nation's best and will present a significant challenge. Tennessee Volunteers (6-2, 3-2) Tennessee has an impressive defense, but the Volunteers also have a talented running back in DeSean Bishop. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow him down, as he can make opposing defenses pay if he gets into a rhythm. Meanwhile, Tennessee's quarterback situation has been a concern, with the Volunteers relying on George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon. The two quarterbacks have different styles. MacIntyre tends to be more conservative, often targeting receivers near or behind the line of scrimmage, while Brandon is more willing to push the ball downfield. It will be interesting to see which quarterback Tennessee turns to on Saturday against Kentucky. At wide receiver, Mike Matthews has emerged as the Volunteers' primary target, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards. Defensively, Tennessee has been impressive, recording 35 sacks, eight interceptions, and nine fumble recoveries this season. Kentucky will need to protect the football and avoid costly mistakes to have a chance to leave Knoxville with a victory. The Wildcats will likely need a near-perfect performance on both sides of the ball. Turnovers could quickly swing the momentum in Tennessee's favor, especially with the Volunteers playing in front of their home crowd at Neyland Stadium. Tennessee had an impressive 26-10 victory over Alabama at home. However, the Volunteers have also suffered a couple of notable losses, including a 20-17 defeat to Texas at home and most recently a heartbreaking 27-24 loss to South Carolina on a game-winning field goal. With both teams coming off a bye week, Kentucky will have an opportunity to prepare for Tennessee's defensive strengths. Still, winning on the road against a talented Volunteers team will be a difficult task. The Wildcats will look to keep that momentum going, improve to 8-1 overall and 6-1 in conference play, and strengthen their case for a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, the challenge does not get any easier this weekend. Kentucky must travel to Knoxville to face a Tennessee team with a dominant defense and plenty of motivation of its own. The Volunteers are also coming off a bye week and will be ready to respond after their loss to South Carolina. While Kentucky has been playing some of its best football of the season, I believe the Wildcats' winning streak comes to an end in a close, low-scoring contest. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. This will still earn a front-and-center spot, though. As good as Tennessee has been – including a relatively dominant 26-10 win over Alabama – it's coming off a 27-24 loss to South Carolina, and it's one loss away from being in a really, really tough spot to stay alive for the CFP. The Volunteer pass rush is the best in the nation, and it should be disruptive in the Kentucky backfield, but it really is about the offense. Tennessee's ground game has been fantastic – it's 16th in the nation – and that's a jumping-off point. Only Vanderbilt and Youngstown State failed to get at least 340 yards against the Kentucky defense. Yes, Kentucky is for real. It's well coached, sharp as a tack, and it's one of those teams that just knows how to win. Week 10, targeting CJ Carr, Micah Gilbert, and Darian Mensah in Saturday's showdown. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Darian Mensah, CJ Carr, NCAAF. South Bend will be the epicenter of the college football universe on Saturday night when the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes roll into town to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. We won't get to see Malachi Toney in action, but our Miami vs. Notre Dame prop picks for this heavyweight bout focus on the showdown between elite quarterbacks Darian Mensah and CJ Carr. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Miami vs. Notre Dame predictions ahead of kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. Best Miami vs Notre Dame props Prop pick #1: CJ Carr Over 4.5 rush attempts I gave out this same prop when Notre Dame faced BYU, and CJ Carr came through. I'm backing it again, up to 55%, for many of the same reasons. It starts with the game plan. This Miami defense ranks second in EPA per rush but 110th in EPA per pass. That means we'll likely see fewer handoffs and more dropback opportunities. That also puts Carr up against a Hurricanes front that ranks 15th in pass-rush grade, per PFF, and 29th nationally in sack rate. Carr has shown this season that he's not afraid to scramble. Factor in sacks counting as rush attempts, and he should clear this total for the fifth time in seven contests. Prop pick #2: Micah Gilbert Over 31.5 receiving yards Jordan Faison leads all Notre Dame receivers with 56 targets, while Jaden Greathouse and Micah Gilbert are tied with 33 targets apiece. But Gilbert is the player being undervalued here, and I'm backing him up to 54%. Miami's secondary isn't just struggling in coverage; it's also struggling to make tackles in the open field. Gilbert has the best yards after catch per reception (5.5) of Carr's top three targets and ranks second behind Faison in yards per route run. Gilbert is also the most reliable of the three, securing 72.7% of his targets. He's averaging 70.4 receiving yards in the six games in which he's run at least 20 routes. He's a bargain with a receiving yards line that's less than half of Faison's 69.5-yard total. Prop pick #3: Darian Mensah Over 1.5 passing touchdowns With Malachi Toney sidelined, Darian Mensah has an opportunity to take another step toward the Heisman tonight, and I'm backing him up to 55% to throw multiple touchdown passes. Not only do the Hurricanes rank third in red-zone scoring, but only Notre Dame has a higher offensive Eckel rate than Miami this season. As well as Notre Dame defends, the Irish are depleted on the back end heading into this game. Defensive captain Drayk Bowen is out at linebacker, and the secondary will be without DJ McKinney and Tae Johnson. The Irish gave up three touchdown passes to UNC's Billy Edwards, one of the few quality passers they've faced this season. Mensah leads the nation in passing efficiency and completion rate, and getting him at this number is a gift. The Hurricanes are No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll as well, but will be an underdog when they go to South Bend to take on the Fighting Irish this weekend. According to Yahoo Sports research, it appears to be the first time that a team ranked No. 1 in the CFP is an underdog against a team ranked outside of the top 10. The Fighting Irish are ranked fourth in the AP poll. Notre Dame was up to a 6.5-point favorite at some sportsbooks on Thursday afternoon, but that number has moved all the way out to -8.5 because of the news that star Miami WR Malachi Toney needs ankle surgery and will miss the game . The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. away.blurb: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish may have caught a break before their showdown with No. 1 Miami, but Marcus Freeman isn’t treating the reported loss of Malachi Toney as a reason to throw out the defensive game plan. In a Thursday report, On3’s Daniel Hager highlighted Freeman’s refusal to assume the Miami receiver would be unavailable. Toney rolled his ankle during Wednesday’s practice, and On3’s Pete Nakos and Brett McMurphy reported he would undergo TightRope surgery and be sidelined indefinitely. A return later in the season remains possible. In Toney’s college debut, he caught six passes for 82 yards and a touchdown as Miami beat Notre Dame 27-24. That result later proved critical when Miami earned a College Football Playoff berth and the Irish were left out. The Irish will be missing defensive help of their own. Linebacker Drayk Bowen is out with an ankle injury, and safety Brauntae Johnson and cornerback DJ McKinney also remain unavailable. Toney, the Hurricanes’ leading receiver and one of college football’s top playmakers, reportedly needs surgery after injuring his ankle Wednesday. He is expected to miss Saturday’s game in South Bend. Freeman, however, says Notre Dame still intends to prepare for him. The conference mandates those reports for conference matchups, and Notre Dame is a nonconference opponent. That leaves the Irish without the usual conference-mandated injury updates on Toney unless Miami voluntarily provides them. Miami confirmed the practice injury Wednesday but did not publicly provide a surgical timetable. ESPN subsequently reported that Toney is expected to miss Notre Dame and likely several more weeks. As ESPN’s Adam Rittenberg reported, Freeman emphasized Miami’s roster depth. “It’s not always the position as much as it is the player,” he said. home.headline: Miami gets concerning Malachi Toney injury update ahead of Notre Dame clash
home.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. More news: CFP Committee Chair Under Fire for Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Toney ranks second in NCAA football with 73 receptions, third with 1,027 receiving yards, and third with 13 touchdowns. The 5-foot-11 sophomore has delivered several impressive performances this past season, including 154 yards and two touchdowns in Miami’s double-overtime win over Florida State. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. Meanwhile, Miami is undefeated, and a loss could hurt its standing in the CFP rankings. Keeping that perfect record could strengthen Miami’s chances of a first-round bye in the CFP. The Miami Hurricanes take on the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. home.headline: Notre Dame’s Marcus Freeman Raises Questions About Miami’s Malachi Toney Status
home.blurb: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish may have caught a break before their showdown with No. 1 Miami, but Marcus Freeman isn’t treating the reported loss of Malachi Toney as a reason to throw out the defensive game plan. In a Thursday report, On3’s Daniel Hager highlighted Freeman’s refusal to assume the Miami receiver would be unavailable. Toney rolled his ankle during Wednesday’s practice, and On3’s Pete Nakos and Brett McMurphy reported he would undergo TightRope surgery and be sidelined indefinitely. A return later in the season remains possible. In Toney’s college debut, he caught six passes for 82 yards and a touchdown as Miami beat Notre Dame 27-24. That result later proved critical when Miami earned a College Football Playoff berth and the Irish were left out. The Irish will be missing defensive help of their own. Linebacker Drayk Bowen is out with an ankle injury, and safety Brauntae Johnson and cornerback DJ McKinney also remain unavailable. Toney, the Hurricanes’ leading receiver and one of college football’s top playmakers, reportedly needs surgery after injuring his ankle Wednesday. He is expected to miss Saturday’s game in South Bend. Freeman, however, says Notre Dame still intends to prepare for him. Notre Dame’s Marcus Freeman Addresses Malachi Toney Injury Uncertainty “We’ll see if he plays or not,” Freeman said. “We have to make sure we have a plan if he plays, if he doesn’t, we’ll adjust.” Miami isn’t required to release an ACC availability report for Saturday’s game. The conference mandates those reports for conference matchups, and Notre Dame is a nonconference opponent. That leaves the Irish without the usual conference-mandated injury updates on Toney unless Miami voluntarily provides them. Miami confirmed the practice injury Wednesday but did not publicly provide a surgical timetable. ESPN subsequently reported that Toney is expected to miss Notre Dame and likely several more weeks. Freeman revealed that he learned of the injury after practice Wednesday, leaving Notre Dame only the final days of preparation to consider an offense without its top receiver. Earlier, Freeman called Toney “one of one,” according to The Associated Press’ Tim Reynolds . Miami’s Malachi Toney Absence Would Test Hurricanes Offense The sophomore has 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games in 2026. Those totals rank second nationally in catches, third in receiving yards and tied for second in touchdown receptions. He accounted for more than a third of Miami’s receptions and receiving yards before the injury. Against North Carolina last Saturday, Toney had seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns in a 38-35 victory. But Freeman isn’t planning on Miami’s offense disappearing without him. As ESPN’s Adam Rittenberg reported, Freeman emphasized Miami’s roster depth. “It’s not always the position as much as it is the player,” he said. Cooper Barkate is Miami’s next-leading receiver with 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns

home.blurb: Which made it all the more gut-wrenching when the Heisman Trophy front-runner came down with an injury during practice the week leading up to the Hurricanes ' mammoth matchup against Notre Dame . Reports said Toney suffered a high ankle sprain on Wednesday, Nov. 4, and that he would undergo surgery, putting not only the showdown with the No. 6 Fighting Irish out of the question, but the rest of his stellar season in jeopardy. Toney has battled injuries throughout the season, briefly leaving games against Wake Forest on Sept. 18, Clemson on Oct. 3, Florida State on Oct. 17 and Pittsburgh on Oct. 24. He never went back to the locker room, though his limited play late against Wake can be explicitly tied to the offense's stagnation and one of their closest games of the season. And he was able to shake off his injury vs. Pitt en route to breaking his own Miami record with 16 catches for 194 yards and three touchdowns. When will Malachi Toney return? According to the Cleveland Clinic , high ankle sprains occur when the ligaments that attach the tibia to the fibula near the foot are torn or damaged. Recovery takes six to eight weeks, though the Clinic says it might take longer for athletes to return to play. However, there is hope Toney can return sooner, with initial reports indicating he could return in time for the College Football Playoff. The first round of the CFP is Dec. 18-19, six weeks away. If Miami retains one of the top four spots in the final CFP rankings (they're No. 1 heading into today's game at Notre Dame), they would first play in the quarterfinals Dec. 30 or Jan. 1, in about eight weeks. There's a chance Toney could return for the ACC championship game Dec. 5, four weeks from now. It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss . So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship. On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Need to know This is the fifth straight time these two have met while ranked: Maybe that doesn't seem like something that's all that impressive to you, but for context, it had happened only five times in the first 46 meetings between the schools. Georgia has had the better end of most meetings, as they lead the series 34-14-1, and a win for Ole Miss this weekend would give the Rebels consecutive wins over the Dawgs for the first time since the 1995 and 1996 seasons. Kirby Smart has done well against ranked opponents: The Georgia coach is 44-18 against AP-ranked teams during his tenure in Athens. That's the fifth-best record by any head coach against ranked teams in AP Poll history (minimum of 20 games). That includes a stretch of six wins in their last seven against ranked teams. The last loss? To Ole Miss in the playoff last year. Trinidad Chambliss could tie a school record here: Chambliss has thrown for at least one touchdown in 21 consecutive games. Our Staff Picks and Final Scores Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) and No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1) are set to square off on Saturday , in what will mark one of the biggest and most consequential games in the history of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Considering what Ole Miss has left in the final quarter of its season, there would be a lot of ground to make up. Ahead of the Rebels' top-10 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss Rebels On SI Staff Predictions Oct 18, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) runs the ball for a touchdown against Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) during the first half of the game at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Galatzan Matt Galatzan The last two times these two teams met, both games were absolute cinema. Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels offense was unstoppable in both matchups, particularly in Round 2, when they knocked of the Bulldogs in the College Football Playoff. This year, the calculus has changed a bit. The Rebels have a new play caller, and new weapons on the outside. The Defense has also been struggling as of late. On the other side, the Bulldogs are built on defense, running the football and controlling the clock - exactly where Ole Miss has been exploited defensively. For Ole Miss to win here, I think Chambliss - especially without Kewan Lacy in the lineup - is going to have to be Superman. We have seen him do it before plenty of times, but if the Bulldogs can deploy a similar game plan that Texas did two weeks ago, it could be a long day. Shekai Mills-Knight could be an X-factor, but it's hard to be able to rely on a redshirt freshman on a stage like this. The Rebels do have an elite home field advantage, but at the end of the day, I think it all comes down to the Rebels defense and if they can hold up against the Georgia run game. I'll take the Dawgs in a tight one. Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27 Understandably, almost everyone had the LSU game circled on Ole Miss’ schedule going into the season. Offensively, Trinidad Chambliss will need to play a game similar to the one he played against LSU all the way back in Week 3. Without Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss will need efficiency from Chambliss, Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight on the ground. The Rebels are 26-1 at home since 2023, including a victory over the Bulldogs in the 2024 regular season that had very similar stakes as this game. Picking any team, let alone one that’s been as hot and cold as Ole Miss has been at times this season, to beat the No. 2 team in the country could age poorly. Despite that, give me Pete Golding, Trinidad Chambliss and the rest of the Ole Miss Rebels to win and keep their playoff and SEC Championship ambitions alive and send the Rebel fans home happy on Saturday night. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks for tonight expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion against Trinidad Chambliss & Co. as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss to the Rebels. Georgia is a 3.5-point favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7, while the total sits at 56.5. Don't miss kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss today: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. If Ole Miss falls behind, Georgia's offense will lean on Gunner Stockton to manage the game and take a ball-control approach against a Rebels defense ranked 88th in the country in EPA per rush. Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Georgia team total Over 30.5 Georgia vs Ole Miss prop: Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Chambliss can only do so much, and against a freakishly athletic and long Georgia defense, I don't think Ole Miss will be scoring at nearly as high a clip as it has against lesser SEC teams. I would take the Under on Ole Miss' team total at 24.5 or better . Georgia linebacker Chris Cole is arguably the best defensive player in the country, and Glenn Schumann and Kirby Smart could deploy him as a Chambliss stopper. With 4.5 40-yard dash speed and nearly 34-inch arms, Cole has earned his nickname of "Tarantula." Look for the Bulldogs to spy Chambliss with him and use him as a blitzer too; he leads Georgia in pressures (24) and pass-rush win rate (17.4%). With Cole hunting Chambliss and the Bulldogs' defense ranking top 20 in rush success rate (37.8%), Ole Miss will struggle to find the end zone.
