picks.blurb: Kirk Herbstreit explains his prediction for Georgia at Ole Miss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Kirk Herbstreit explains his prediction for Georgia at Ole Miss James Morgan, UGA Wire · UGA Wire Sat, November 7, 2026 at 5:40 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads ESPN "College GameDay" host Kirk Herbstreit made predictions for all of the top Week 10 college football games (outside of the game he is commentating). Herbstreit along with the rest of the GameDay desk predicted who woudl win an SEC showdown between the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs and the No. 10 Ole Miss Rebels. Herbstreit picked Georgia to beat Ole Miss. He explained why he thinks the Dawgs will win to get revenge for losing to Ole Miss and quarterback Trinidad Chambliss in the Sugar Bowl last season. "Ole Miss has won 16 games in a row at home," Herbstreit said. The Rebels have not lost at home since falling to Kentucky in 2024. Chambliss is undefeated at home. "I think Gunner Stockton wins this game," Herbstreit continued. "Lots of short, quick passes, get the ball out of his hands." Herbstreit notes that the Ole Miss defense has been struggling to tackle and thinks that is a matchup that Georgia could take advantage of. Herbstreit along with Desmond Howard, former Alabama coach Nick Saban and actor Jason Sudeikis all picked Georgia to win. Pat McAfee was the only one to pick Ole Miss to win in what he describes as "Trinidad's last stand" this season. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL Week 9 updates Luka has tight back Rivers to coach NC State CFB winners and losers Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. away.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable. His status with the program will be re-evaluated after this week's contest," per a statement from a program spokesperson. Sumrall added what he called his "official VB3 statement": "He wants to play. It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton. home.headline: Scouting report, prediction as Florida football hosts Oklahoma
home.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going? home.blurb: It was a busy injury report week for the Sooners, but they'll have a few players available who had popped up on the report this week. Wide receivers Jer'Michael Carter and Elijah Thomas, tight end Rocky Beers, offensive lineman Jake Maikkula, defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu, and defensive back Eli Bowen have been cleared to play against Florida. Two key players are game-time decisions against the Gators. Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis and defensive back Peyton Bowen still have their statuses up in the air as kickoff in The Swamp approaches. The Gators got some good news, as wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo are available for this game. Florida will be without wide receiver Vernell Brown III, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji, defensive lineman Jeremiah McCloud, and inside linebacker Jaden Robinson. For the Sooners, that means they'll have their full complement of skill-position players available Saturday night, except for Harris and Washington. The offensive line is still banged up without Fodje and possibly Pierre-Louis, the two projected starting guards coming into the year, but the five-man unit of Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris is the healthiest the o-line has been in weeks. home.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Florida injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting Starting center Jake Maikkula was removed from the availability report after missing last week against South Carolina. Left tackle Michael Fasusi is also still healthy since his return two weeks ago. That leaves OU without only Ryan Fodje, who will miss his third game in a row. The Sooners also got good news on the defensive side of the ball, with cornerback Eli Bowen set to return after missing the last four games. S Peyton Bowen: GAME-TIME DECISION Safety Peyton Bowen was also listed on the injury report last week before ultimately being available against South Carolina. Hopefully, it's the same conclusion this week but he's even healthier, because Bowen is a vital piece of OU's defense as one of 15 semifinalists for the Jim Thorpe Award, which goes to the best defensive back in college football. Replacement: If Bowen can't go, Michael Boganowski should get the start after also starting last week, even with Bowen available. Florida's QB play won't be as good, but Boganowski made some early mistakes against South Carolina, so the Sooners need Bowen out there. OL Eddy Pierre-Louis: GAME-TIME DECISION Offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis hasn't seen the field since Week 4 against Georgia because of an injury. It looks like he will miss another one on Saturday, meaning he's officially been out more games than he's played this season after starting at guard the first three weeks. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas, who was listed as probable on Friday, will make his return after missing the past two games. He's caught five passes for 49 yards this season. ILB Jaden Robinson: out OL Emeka Ugorji: out TE Evan Chieca: out DL Jeramiah McCloud: out WR Vernell Brown III: out It's been a week of change for the Oklahoma Sooners, including players actually getting healthier instead of getting worse on the availability report. Newly appointed interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten will get the rare occurrence in Norman of having nearly his entire starting offensive line healthy for his play-calling debut against No. 24 Florida on Saturday night. That alone should have OU's offense looking better after Ben Arbuckle was fired on Monday. OU, though, can still never go a week without a lengthy injured list.
